title: As a developer, I can send a transactional email with one documented API call — minimal required fields, copy-paste quickstart code, and a message id back for tracking
As a developer, I can send a batch of personalized emails in a single API request with per-message status in the response, instead of looping one call per recipient
As a platform engineer, I can retry a failed send safely — idempotency keys or documented duplicate-suppression semantics guarantee a network timeout never double-sends a receipt
As a developer, I can schedule an email for future delivery through the API and cancel it before it goes out
As a developer, I can authenticate my sending domain end to end — the product generates the exact SPF/DKIM/DMARC DNS records, verifies them, and exposes verification status via the API
As a deliverability manager, I can see bounce, complaint, and engagement analytics with guidance on inbox placement and sender reputation, not just raw counts
As a platform engineer, I can read and manage bounce, complaint, and unsubscribe suppression lists via the API so my app never re-emails a hard bounce
As a deliverability manager, I can get dedicated IPs with documented warmup — automated ramp-up or a published warmup schedule — when my volume outgrows shared pools
As a developer, I can create, version, and update email templates through the API and trigger sends by template id with variable payloads
As a developer, I can personalize emails with a documented templating language — merge fields, conditionals, loops — and preview or test-render a template before sending
As a developer, I can author emails as code — React Email, MJML, or an equivalent maintained framework the vendor documents first-party — and keep templates in version control
As a platform engineer, I can receive webhooks for delivered, bounced, and complained events with documented retry behavior, so my app reacts to email outcomes in real time
As a platform engineer, I can verify webhook authenticity — signed payloads with documented signature verification code — so spoofed events can't poison my delivery state
As a developer, I can track opens and clicks and query a per-message event history via the API to answer 'what happened to this email?'
As a developer, I can receive email — point MX records at the service and get parsed messages (headers, body, attachments) delivered to my webhook or API
As a developer, I can route inbound mail with rules — match on recipient or pattern and forward, store, or POST to different endpoints
As a developer, I can go from signup to my first delivered email in minutes — the quickstart is copy-paste complete for my language and doesn't hide required setup
As a developer, I can test sends without delivering real email — a sandbox domain, test mode, or test API keys that accept messages and fire events, safe for CI and agents
As a developer, I can send through a documented SMTP relay with generated credentials when my framework or legacy app can't call the REST API
As a platform engineer, I can isolate tenants — subaccounts, subusers, or multiple domains with separate credentials, suppression lists, and reputation — for the platform I'm building
As a platform engineer, I can find the documented throughput and rate limits — requests per second, burst behavior, and the headers or errors that signal throttling
As a founder, I can price the service from the public site alone — per-volume tiers, overage rates, and add-on costs (dedicated IPs, validation) published without a sales call
As a founder, I can integrate and validate the service on a free tier or trial that allows real deliveries to my own users, not just a demo
